page: Amazon Web Services c5d.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The configuration provides 16 vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). For system memory, the instance is equipped with 32 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA, although newer vector accelerators like AVX-512 VNNI and AMX are not supported. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units.

A defining characteristic of the c5d family is the inclusion of integrated instance storage. The c5d.4xlarge bundles a 400 GB local NVMe SSD, providing low-latency ephemeral storage without requiring external network-attached volumes for temporary scratch space. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 5 Gbps. By coupling high-speed local block storage directly to dedicated compute resources, the instance achieves operational cost efficiency for workloads that repeatedly ingest and purge intermediate working sets, eliminating external storage egress and provisioning overheads.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable middle-tier multi-threaded processing. Multi-core performance in stress-ng (14,734.77) and Geekbench (7,156.0) align with the median 50% across surveyed instances. Application benchmarks reflect consistent execution throughput, showing 12,847.0 in Clang software compilation, 12.39 GB/sec in static web serving, and 15.63 million operations per second during Redis SET operations. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into the bottom 25%, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1,122.0 and stress-ng reaching 1,405.49. Data decompression also trails, with single- and multi-threaded bzip3 rates lagging behind higher-tier architectures.

Given its hardware topology and benchmark profiles, the c5d.4xlarge is suited for CPU-bound batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed memory caching, and ETL workloads that rely on fast temporary NVMe scratch space. It is less suited for memory-intensive in-memory databases requiring high memory-to-vCPU ratios or large language model inference beyond compact parameter sets.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores, 32 GB of DDR4 memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and an integrated 400 GB local NVMe SSD for fast temporary scratch space. With a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps and absence of dedicated GPUs, it prioritizes reliable CPU compute and low-latency local storage. Benchmarks place its multi-core capabilities in the mid-tier category, evidenced by solid scores in PassMark CPU tests, software compilation, and a throughput of 15.63 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core processing and large compression tasks show modest lower-quartile performance. The instance provides a cost-efficient balance between compute density and high-speed local disk I/O, making it well fitted for continuous integration builds, distributed caching, batch processing, and data transformations requiring scratch storage.
